text:
An unlawful homicide committed by a minister acting as an organ of the state is an act jure imperii. The ICJ in Germany v. Italy held that grave illegality does not turn a sovereign act into one jure gestionis, and a purely personal killing is a private act outside state immunity rather than a commercial jure gestionis act. Such conduct can still attract immunity, so it is not the case that it never does.

CONFIDENCE: 84
